verdict.rationale: ImageMagick is a C library and CLI that developers embed in their own applications through bindings for C, C++, Python, .NET and Node.js, build from source, and run on Linux, Windows and macOS. Its security policies are designed for operators' own server environments. Community reports corroborate this: a SaaS runs it on its own Windows servers, users deployed it on Heroku, and it is described as mostly shipped inside other apps. Missing for 10: no evidence of an official container image or a first-party server/daemon mode.

support.subject: As a developer, the conversion engine runs inside my own infrastructure as a library, container, or server I operate

citations.quote: Extensive APIs Bindings for C, C++, Python, .NET, Node.js.
Developers can integrate ImageMagick into applications to perform tasks such as resizing, color correction, format conversion, and complex image transformations.
It is written in C and can be used on a variety of operating systems, including Linux, Windows, and macOS.
Tailor security policies to suit your server environment.
